description.value: The study compared hemodynamic brain responses and task-related functional connectivity between big wave surfers and non-big wave surfers while they viewed positive and negative IAPS images differing in arousal.

design.value: A convenience sample of 25 surfers was categorized into big wave surfers (BWS, n = 15) and non-big wave surfers (CON, n = 10). After one withdrawal for claustrophobia and one exclusion for falling asleep during the scan, 23 participants were included in the analyses. Participants completed an event-related fMRI task involving randomized presentation of 160 affective images and 20 fixation trials. Group-level analyses used a 2 (group) by 2 (arousal) by 2 (valence) ANOVA, post-hoc one-sample and two-sample t-tests, and generalized psychophysiological interaction analyses.

task_description.value: Participants viewed a series of images from the International Affective Picture System while undergoing brain fMRI. Images were categorized according to valence and arousal ratings into high arousal positive, high arousal negative, low arousal positive, and low arousal negative groups. Forty images were selected from each group, for a total of 160 images, with 20 additional fixation trials.

design_type.value: event-related design with jittered inter-stimulus interval

instructions.value: Participants were asked to view all images presented on the screen. No tasks related to regulation were instructed.

stimuli.value: IAPS photographs; all photographs were first edited to reduce saturation by 30%. Images were presented through MRI-compatible goggles.

task_performance_measures.value: No behavioral responses, such as button presses, were performed; no real-time subjective valence or arousal ratings were performed.

instrument.value: 3 T MRI scanner (Achieva, Philips, Best, Netherlands)

description.value: A 7-min anatomical MRI scan was completed. Anatomical images of the functional slice locations were obtained with gradient echo sequences in the sagittal plane with TR = 8.1 ms, TE = 3.7 ms, bandwidth = 191.4 Hz/pixel, flip angle = 8°, field of view = 240 × 240 mm, matrix = 240 × 240, 145 slices with slice thickness = 1 mm and no gap.

instrument.value: 3 T MRI scanner (Achieva, Philips, Best, Netherlands)

description.value: Functional BOLD signals were acquired with a multi-shot gradient echo echoplanar imaging (EPI) sequence. Twenty-two axial slices covering the whole brain were acquired with TR = 2000 ms, TE = 30 ms, bandwidth = 56.6 Hz/pixel, flip angle = 75°, field of view = 240 × 240 mm, matrix = 64 × 62, 22 slices with slice thickness = 5 mm and no gap.

mr_acquisition_type.value: axial slices covering the whole brain

description.value: Images of each individual subject were realigned and corrected for slice timing. A mean functional image volume was constructed for each subject per run, co-registered with the high-resolution structural image, segmented for normalization with affine registration followed by nonlinear transformation, and smoothed with an 8-mm Gaussian kernel at full width at half maximum.

steps.value: Construction of a mean functional image volume for each subject per run from the realigned image volumes

Spatial smoothing with a Gaussian kernel of 8 mm at full width at half maximum
Exclusion of subjects whose head motion exceeded 3.0 mm in translation or 3 degrees in rotation

hrf_model.value: canonical hemodynamic response function with its temporal derivative

model_settings.value: Image onset in each trial was convolved with the canonical hemodynamic response function and its temporal derivative. Realignment parameters in all six dimensions were entered as regressors. Data were high-pass filtered with a 1/128 Hz cutoff, and serial autocorrelation was corrected by a first-degree autoregressive or AR(1) model. First-level contrasts were HAP vs. FIX, HAN vs. FIX, LAP vs. FIX, LAN vs. FIX, HAP vs. LAP, and HAN vs. LAN.

level.value: first-level analysis for each individual subject

estimator.value: The GLM estimated the component of variance that could be explained by each regressor.

model_type.value: 2 (group) by 2 (arousal) by 2 (valence) ANOVA model with one-sample and two-sample t-tests

model_settings.value: Contrast images from individual-level analyses were used. The ANOVA examined main effects of group, arousal, and valence as well as the interaction effect. Post-hoc analyses used one-sample t-tests across all 23 surfers and two-sample t-tests between BWS and CON.

The hemodynamic responses of HAP, HAN, LAP, LAN, and FIX formed the psychological regressors. Extracted mean BOLD time series were temporally filtered, mean corrected, and de-convolved to generate neural signal time series for each seed mask. These time series were multiplied by the onset times of HAP, HAN, LAP, LAN, and FIX separately and re-convolved with the canonical hemodynamic response function to obtain the PPI variables. The psychological regressors, physiological variable, and PPI variables were entered in a whole-brain GLM. Brain regions showing significant BWS versus CON differences were used as seed regions.

level.value: individual-subject generalized PPI followed by random-effect group analysis
